body:
A signal that only fires when `seek()` is called has no practical point. Also, note that the current time may advance even outside of `seek()` calls.

While a signal fired by `seek_internal()`, which is called internally in many places, might have some meaning, `seek()` is not a function used internally.

Incidentally, if `seek_internal()` triggers a signal and `AnimationPlayerEditor` subscribes to it, an infinite loop could potentially occur. As this example illustrates, this implementation has inverted dependencies.

In other words, this signal is only required by the AnimationPlayerEditor to subscribe to it, the user script side does not need it because it can implement its own wrapper function like `seek_with_signal()` to fire any signal it wants.

---

The fundamental issue likely lies in `AnimationPlayerEditor` not being easily accessible from editor script. If `AnimationPlayerEditor` becomes available in editor script, it would simply involve actively calling `AnimationPlayerEditor._seek_value_changed()` immediately after calling `seek()`.

This inaccessible issue has been pointed out before like https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/3468.

We know there is a certain demand for accessing AnimationPlayerEditor. So, rather than piling on stop-gap measures like placing signals on every individual function, the focus should be on exposing `AnimationPlayerEditor` related editor classes with a clean/safe API.
